label: Bible Study
prompt: Yea, though I walk through the _____ of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
verse: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
note: The shepherd psalm turns dark here — but notice the walk is THROUGH the valley, not into it.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: After these things the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy _____, and thy exceeding great reward.
verse: After these things the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.
note: Abram gets no timetable, just a shield and a reward — and that was enough to believe.

label: Sunday School
prompt: I do set my _____ in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
verse: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
note: The KJV never says 'rainbow' — God simply sets his 'bow' in the cloud, a weapon hung up in peace.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my _____, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested.
verse: And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested.
note: The prayer of Jabez: 'coast' is KJV for territory — he asked God to move his fences outward.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the _____ of his friend.
verse: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
note: Everyone quotes 'sharpens another'; the KJV sharpens 'the countenance of his friend.'
